behaviorNotes: The browser owns the top layer, ::backdrop, Escape ordering and background inertness; the app wrapper only adds controlled close, focus loop/restore, backdrop pointer dismissal and scroll locking.

Escape is handled in the dialog keydown with stopPropagation + preventDefault, so native cancel is suppressed and Twin window shortcuts never see the event; the cancel listener only handles browser/AT-initiated close requests and keeps them controlled.
Scroll locking is reference-counted across nested dialogs with root-overflow restore and scrollbar-width compensation.
Focus restore keeps the pre-showModal activeElement fallback for URL/store-driven dialogs and detached openers that native close() cannot restore.
ModalTitle remains the accessible-name seam through context + aria-labelledby, including asChild titles.
The portalContainer seam and both page-level container states were deleted: DOM ancestry now carries theme variables, and the Twin page keeps GPU rendering while the dialog is in the top layer.
residualRisks: jsdom 30 does not implement HTMLDialogElement.showModal/close, so unit tests exercise the wrapper plus an attribute fallback; native top-layer behavior is covered only by the Chrome 155 probes.
Cross-browser modal behavior (Safari/Firefox) was not re-run in this round.
The WebGPU Twin probe is headless Chrome with d3d11; the YMS tabs share the same Modal wrapper but were not separately browser-probed.
